title: PokéPath TD Route 1-1 Guide — Shaymin at Wave 100
heading: Route 1-1: how to beat Shaymin
description: Keep damage on Shaymin after Natural Cure removes your status effects. If its health climbs between attacks, move a sustained attacker into range of a longer stretch of the path.
answer: Keep damage on Shaymin after Natural Cure removes your status effects. If its health climbs between attacks, move a sustained attacker into range of a longer stretch of the path.
sections: Choose your tiles before the late waves

The opening map has seven field, seven grass, five water and just one mountain tile. Use X on desktop to show ranges before committing that mountain spot. Wave 24 sends 30 Doduo and wave 36 sends 50. If the last birds escape while the first fall quickly, try a second firing window or bouncing attacks before spending on single-target power.

Wave 99 mixes Trevenant and Chansey with Illumise and Volbeat. Wave 100 sends Shaymin alone. Its 120,000 HP regenerate at 1,000 per second. Watch what happens when your lead attacker loses range. A short burst followed by an empty stretch gives that regeneration time to undo your work.

Natural Cure periodically clears status conditions. A Burn starter can still help, but check whether direct hits keep driving the health bar down after the effect disappears. If you already clear wave 99 reliably, keep that lineup and adjust one attacker's position for the final fight.

To recruit Shaymin, defeat it with your attacking Pokémon unequipped. The Lopunny line is exempt. For a first clear, equipment is available unless you have separately enabled a challenge that restricts it.

For other collection requirements see hidden Pokémon unlocks. For roster substitutions use the team role guide.
Replay a cleared wave with the Bicycle

Segmental’s Bicycle costs 1,000,000,000 in the shop. Before buying it for a particular route, check that you have beaten its wave-100 boss. On a cleared map, the Wave Manager appears beside your team at the lower left. Choose the wave there, or use R beside the manager to repeat the current wave. Owning the Bicycle alone does not skip an uncleared boss.

Bicycle shop entry ↗ (new tab) · Wave Manager instructions ↗ (new tab)

For gold farming, give Meowth ↗ (new tab) or Persian a field or grass tile where it can hit repeatedly. Greed pays 10% of the target’s gold per hit. Compare two repeatable waves by recording your balance before and after the same number of minutes. Include time spent restarting a failed attempt. The better wave for your roster is the one that actually earns more per minute.

Check individual waves in the Route 1-1 map ↗ (new tab), resistances in the Shaymin bestiary entry ↗ (new tab) and recruitment in the non-shop unlock guide ↗ (new tab). Placement advice follows these mechanics. A successful clear with a specific roster has not been tested here.

title: PokéPath TD Route 3-3 Guide — Regigigas at Wave 100
heading: Route 3-3: how to beat Regigigas
description: Plan for two different failures on Route 3-3. Groups can overwhelm your coverage before the final wave. Regigigas arrives alone with a billion armor, a billion HP and increasing speed.
answer: Plan for two different failures on Route 3-3. Groups can overwhelm your coverage before the final wave. Regigigas arrives alone with a billion armor, a billion HP and increasing speed.
sections: Choose your tiles before the late waves

There are eight field tiles, six grass tiles, two mountain tiles and no water tiles. Check the terrain before copying a roster from a different map. Wave 87 brings twelve Walrein alongside Sealeo and Spheal. If the pack leaks here, keep group damage aimed at a stretch several enemies occupy together.

Wave 99 contains ten Walrein. Once those fall, wave 100 replaces the pack with Regigigas. Slow Start makes it accelerate. Put your armor specialist where it can begin hitting early. Excadrill can use field or mountain terrain and deals double damage against armor.

Regigigas resists Stun, while its bestiary entry lists Slow, Burn and Poison as effective. If the boss leaves range with armor remaining, try Slow within reach of the armor attacker. If armor falls early but the boss survives, compare sustained damage along the remaining path. A slot spent on Stun alone contributes little to this fight.

To recruit Regigigas, select Tough Enemies at +50% and defeat it. A normal kill or the +25% setting misses that condition. Keep your first-clear roster as a baseline before attempting the larger health and armor pools.

For other collection requirements see hidden Pokémon unlocks. For roster substitutions use the team role guide.

For the rest of the world, compare the Regi bosses before carrying this team over to another map.

Check individual waves in the Route 3-3 map ↗ (new tab), resistances in the Regigigas bestiary entry ↗ (new tab) and recruitment in the non-shop unlock guide ↗ (new tab). Placement advice follows these mechanics. A successful clear with a specific roster has not been tested here.

title: PokéPath TD Route 5-1 Guide — Tapu Koko at Wave 100
heading: Route 5-1: how to beat Tapu Koko
description: Bring a stun source and place your strongest attacker where their ranges overlap. Above half health, Tapu Koko can take damage only while stunned.
answer: Bring a stun source and place your strongest attacker where their ranges overlap. Above half health, Tapu Koko can take damage only while stunned.
sections: Choose your tiles before the late waves

Route 5-1 has five field tiles, four grass, two water and two mountain. There is one path. Look for a stretch where your stun source and your damage dealers can all reach the same target. Wave 99 mixes Clawitzer, Corsola, Cramorant, Wiglett and Staryu. Group coverage that clears this pack can still leave a gap against the lone boss.

Tapu Koko starts with 50,000 HP and no armor. Electrogenesis doubles stun duration. Above 25,000 HP, watch for damage during each stun. If the boss stops moving but its health barely changes, move a damage dealer into that part of the path. If it never stops, check that your control ability actually applies Stun. The boss resists Slow.

Once the boss reaches half health, the stun-only damage condition ends. Keep an attacker covering the exit if it routinely gets through with a sliver of health. Compare attempts at the same difficulty before changing levels or adding a second stun source.

Recruiting Tapu Koko requires a kill with at most three stuns. Count applications from every team member. If you consume the allowance early, narrow the stun coverage to the part of the path with the highest damage, then rely on ordinary attacks for the second half.

For other collection requirements see hidden Pokémon unlocks. For roster substitutions use the team role guide.

Check individual waves in the Route 5-1 map ↗ (new tab), resistances in the Tapu Koko bestiary entry ↗ (new tab) and recruitment in the non-shop unlock guide ↗ (new tab). Placement advice follows these mechanics. A successful clear with a specific roster has not been tested here.

title: PokéPath TD Secret Pokémon — Hidden Triggers and Unlock Checks
heading: Where to find hidden Pokémon in PokéPath TD
description: Find hidden Pokémon by route, settings and reward type. Check normal mode, wave repeat, map victory and save-linked codes before retrying.
answer: For scenery secrets, leave Challenge mode and wait between waves. For a hidden boss map, turn wave repeat off and close the victory screen after winning to collect the Pokémon.
sections: Start with a route you already have

Greavard · Route 1-3
Click the open grave between waves. You can look for it independently of the Lunala fight.
Cacnea · Route 2-2
Click the cactus in the upper-left corner.
Dhelmise or Manaphy · Route 3-4
The boat gives Dhelmise. The cave leads to Manaphy, which you must defeat inside.
Ducklett · Route 4-2
Look in the water for the egg.
Sandygast · Route 5-1
Click the sandcastle on the beach. Beating Tapu Koko is a separate unlock.

For Calyrex, click the chessboard on Route 8-2 between waves, then win the Board Room fight. On Route 8-1, Galarian Farfetch’d has a different entrance condition: let Klefki escape during wave 50, enter the castle and defeat Sirfetch’d.
Three secrets you can check away from the path

• Chatot. Outside Challenge mode, set Master volume to 0, Music to 4, Interface to 4 and Effects to 1. Note your own settings before changing them.
  • Luvdisc. Open Profile and click the Ho-Oh or Keldeo achievement badge. A locked badge still works.
  • Tyrunt. Open the Secrets tutorial in the Compendium and click its picture.
If you are looking for a shiny instead

Deploy Smeargle and let it hit enemies. Its ability can affect final evolutions you own, including Pokémon in the box. The project FAQ ↗ (new tab) gives the chance per hit as about 1 in 9,000, rising to 1 in 3,000 with Shiny Charm. An unevolved target cannot benefit. Each hit is another chance, so the published odds do not set a deadline for a particular shiny.

If clicking scenery does nothing, check the route number, mode and whether a wave is running. If you won a cave fight but the Pokémon is missing, turn off repeat and dismiss the victory screen. For MissingNo. and other website rewards, use the Player code from the save that will receive the reward. The redemption guide shows the two fields.

If the target is a regular route boss, look up its extra condition before replaying 100 waves. Regigigas needs a specific difficulty, while Shaymin checks equipment. The project’s 1.7.3 unlock list ↗ (new tab) includes later routes, puzzles and special evolutions. These instructions were checked against the list; individual rewards have not been claimed here.

title: PokéPath TD Route Bosses — Clear and Recruitment Conditions
heading: Route boss counters and recruitment conditions
description: Compare wave-100 boss defenses with their recruitment conditions across Worlds 1–5. Choose terrain, damage and status effects for the reward you want.
answer: Pick your goal before equipping the team. A setup that wins the fight can miss the recruitment reward: Moltres is easier to damage from far away, but recruiting it requires most of your direct damage to land inside its ring.
sections:
Route 1-2 · Celebi ↗ (new tab)
Teleports back, sheds residual damage and heals 7,000 HP. Move direct damage toward the first waypoint. To recruit: Finish within 7.5 seconds of combat after the first waypoint.
Route 1-4 · Zapdos ↗ (new tab)
Nearby attackers may lose attacks to paralysis. Use longer reach and cover its armor. To recruit: Allow at most three paralysis effects.
Route 2-1 · Moltres ↗ (new tab)
Nearby attacks deal half damage. Try a longer firing distance for an ordinary clear. To recruit: Deal direct damage equal to at least 88% of its maximum HP from inside the fiery ring.
Route 2-2 · Regirock ↗ (new tab)
Each incoming hit loses 200 damage. Try fewer, stronger hits when rapid attacks barely register. To recruit: Leave Poison, Burn, Nightmare and Scorch off the attacking team.
Route 2-3 · Groudon ↗ (new tab)
At half health it gains 75,000 armor and becomes invulnerable for three seconds. Keep armor damage in range after the transition. To recruit: Keep attacks off Grass tiles.

For the opening map see Shaymin. On Route 1-3, count reveals when attempting to recruit Lunala.

Route 3-1 · Registeel ↗ (new tab)
Hits above 1,000 are reduced. Try faster attacks if large hits are underperforming. To recruit: Keep every single hit at or below 500.
Route 3-2 · Regice ↗ (new tab)
It ignores critical damage and has 200,000 armor. Watch armor loss when comparing attackers. To recruit: Let it block at least 50 critical hits before the kill.
Route 3-4 · Articuno ↗ (new tab)
Nearby attackers take 50% longer to recharge. Check whether a longer-range placement gets more attacks. To recruit: Finish with Hail active.
Route 4-1 · Kyogre ↗ (new tab)
Plan for a three-second invulnerable phase and 75,000 new armor below half HP. To recruit: Land the final blow from a Field tile.
Route 4-3 · Tapu Fini ↗ (new tab)
After eight hits it dodges the next three. Time large hits around the dodge sequence. To recruit: Allow at most ten dodged attacks.
Route 4-4 · Nihilego ↗ (new tab)
Deal damage from Water tiles. Check where the attacker is actually standing. To recruit: Use only attackers whose deployment terrain is exclusively Water.

Regigigas needs the +50% Tough Enemies setting for recruitment.

Route 5-2 · Tapu Bulu ↗ (new tab)
It regenerates 20,000 HP per second. Hits from healing-capable Pokémon cut regeneration by 1,000 per second apiece. To recruit: Leave regeneration intact and concentrate damage.
Route 5-3 · Tapu Lele ↗ (new tab)
An item holder deals 35% less damage. An empty-handed attacker deals 15% more. Compare the same attacker unequipped. To recruit: Use attackers with Power of 100 or less.
Route 5-4 · Keldeo ↗ (new tab)
Burn, Poison, Stun and Slow each grant it a 5,000 shield when applied. Inspect passive effects as well as direct attacks. To recruit: Keep Justified inactive.

For Route 5-1, use the Tapu Koko stun-window guide.
When the challenge selector is locked

The project FAQ ↗ (new tab) lists three prerequisites: earn 540 stars, own at least 30 Pokémon in your box and defeat the wave-100 boss on the map in question. If challenges appear on one route but not another, check the second route’s boss clear.

Each linked bestiary entry describes the enemy. The project unlock guide ↗ (new tab) lists the separate recruit conditions, including bosses beyond this selection. The placement suggestions follow those mechanics; clears were not tested here.
